verdict: Qualcomm's revenue slipped 3% to $10.6B as handset chips fell 13%, but a $5.1B tax benefit from releasing a valuation allowance lifted GAAP profit to $7.37B — a paper gain, not operating performance.

kpis.label: Automotive revenue
kpis.note: +38% YoY, a record at the time

segments.name: QCT
segments.note: The chip business. Inside it: Handsets $6,024M (−13% YoY), Automotive $1,326M (+38%), IoT $1,726M (+9%).

segments.name: QTL
segments.note: Licensing phone makers to use Qualcomm's patents — very high margin (72% pre-tax).

segments.name: Other and reconciling items
segments.note: QSI strategic investments and corporate items not in QCT or QTL; the difference between segment revenue and the reported total.

opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Building chips, modems and AI platforms; up 11% YoY.

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative
opex.note: Selling, legal costs and running the company; up 27% YoY.

opex.name: Other
opex.note: Restructuring and restructuring-related charges of $29M (10-Q) — a one-time cost Qualcomm excludes from its non-GAAP results.

otherDetail: Investment and other income, net of $94M, less $171M of interest expense — a net $77M non-operating expense.
oneTimers: GAAP results include a $5.7B income-tax benefit ($5.33 a share) from releasing a valuation allowance set up in Q4 FY25, after new corporate alternative minimum tax guidance — the entire reason GAAP EPS ($6.88) dwarfs non-GAAP EPS ($2.65). The total tax benefit on the income statement is $5,138M.
The $29M 'Other' operating-expense line is restructuring and restructuring-related charges (10-Q) — excluded from non-GAAP results.
footerNote: Qualcomm guided Q3 FY26 in its release; see the release for the outlook.

takeaways.title: Handsets dragged
takeaways.text: Handset chip revenue fell to $6.02B in a challenging memory environment — the whole reason total revenue slipped 3% despite growth elsewhere.

takeaways.title: Cars keep climbing
takeaways.text: Automotive chip revenue set a record at $1.33B and IoT grew 9% to $1.73B — combined, the two grew 20% YoY as diversification beyond phones continued.

takeaways.title: A tax paper gain
takeaways.text: Releasing a deferred-tax valuation allowance added a $5.7B benefit — profit on paper that brought no cash with it. Underlying non-GAAP profit was $2.84B, down 10% YoY.

sources.label: Form 10-Q for the quarter ended Mar 29, 2026 (SEC EDGAR)

follow100Note: Qualcomm kept $69.53 of every $100 on paper (rows rounded to cents) — almost all of the extra is the one-time $5.1B tax benefit; without it, profit would have been about $21 per $100.
